title: What Goes on in the Brain When a Good Buzz Gets Harshed - Nautilus
gist: Northwestern University neuroscientists used Pfizer's 1974 synthetic cannabinoid CP55940 — about 40 times stronger than THC — to show in a Nature study that intoxicated mice freeze rather than investigate predator scent, offering clues to what happens in the brain during cannabis-induced anxiety.

insights.claim: In 1974 Pfizer developed a synthetic cannabinoid that mimicked THC but was about 40 times stronger; it was never marketed and is instead used to test THC effects in lab animals.
insights.speaker: Jake Currie
insights.so_what: Shows pharma shelved potent cannabinoid agonists — relevant to the cannabinoid drug development landscape.
insights.quote: Pfizer developed a synthetic cannabinoid that mimicked the effects of tetrahydrocannabinol (THC), but was around 40 times stronger

insights.claim: Cannabis can be relaxing but can also produce anxiety, and mice experience the same dual response, enabling study of the brain during a 'bad trip'.
insights.speaker: Jake Currie
insights.so_what: Understanding the anxiety pathway could inform safer cannabinoid therapeutics.

insights.claim: Northwestern University neuroscientists dosed mice with CP55940 and exposed them to fox urine; control mice approached, sniffed and fled, while intoxicated mice resisted investigating and froze more often.
insights.speaker: Jake Currie
insights.so_what: Behavioral evidence that high-dose cannabinoids heighten fear responses — relevant to cannabis product potency debates.
insights.quote: Mice under the influence of CP55940, on the other hand, resisted the urge to investigate and tended to freeze more often.

themes.theme: Toward the neural basis of bad trips

insights.claim: The Nature study suggests scientists may now know what goes on in the brain during a cannabis bad trip.
insights.speaker: Jake Currie
insights.so_what: Mechanistic insight could guide development of cannabinoid drugs that avoid anxiety side effects.
insights.quote: Now scientists might know what’s going on in the brain during a bad trip.
